set: Practice Set 9 (version before the GK update)

sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Scattered through the hills of the western coast are small patches of forest that no one cuts. They belong to a village deity, and custom forbids taking so much as a fallen branch. Some are no larger than a playground. Inside them stand trees older than any in the surrounding country, and beneath the trees a spring that runs when the wells below have failed.

For a long time such groves were described as superstition, and their protection as an obstacle to the rational use of land. The description missed what the custom achieved. A rule against cutting, enforced by belief and by the eye of every neighbour, had preserved a seed bank, a water source and a refuge for birds and small animals at no cost to any government. The villagers did not explain it in those terms. They did not need to; the rule worked whether or not anyone could give the reason for it.

That strength is also the grove's weakness. A protection that rests on belief lasts only as long as the belief does. Where younger people no longer fear the deity, or where a temple of cement replaces the open shrine and needs a car park, the trees go quickly. Law can step in, and sometimes has. But a forest guard posted from outside is a poorer watchman than a village that believes it is being watched.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: A public hearing is held so that people affected by a project may say what they think before it is approved. In practice it often becomes a contest of loudness. The promoters arrive with supporters, the opponents with slogans, and the presiding officer spends three hours keeping order. At the end a report is written recording that objections were raised and replied to, and both sides go home convinced that nothing was heard.

The fault lies less with the participants than with the timing. By the day of the hearing the design is finished, the land identified, and a good deal of money spent. An objection can then be met in only two ways: by rejecting it, or by abandoning the project. Since the second is unthinkable to those who have come so far, the first is nearly certain, and the villagers sense this before they enter the hall.

Consultation works when it comes early enough to change something. If residents are asked where a road should not go before the line is drawn, an engineer can often move it at little cost. People who see their remark alter a plan, even slightly, behave differently at the next meeting. They bring information instead of slogans, because they have learnt that information is used. A hearing held after the decision teaches the opposite lesson, and teaches it thoroughly.

questions.q: What custom protects the groves described in the passage?
opts: Only dead wood may be collected
Nothing may be taken from them, not even a fallen branch
Only the priest may enter them
Trees may be cut once in ten years
questions.why: Custom forbids taking so much as a fallen branch.

questions.q: The earlier description of the groves as 'superstition' was mistaken because it:
opts: exaggerated the age of the trees
assumed the groves were very large
overlooked the practical benefits the custom secured
questions.why: The description missed what the custom achieved: a seed bank, a water source and a wildlife refuge at no public cost.

questions.q: 'They did not need to' means that the villagers:
opts: did not have to understand the ecological reasons for the rule to work
did not need the grove's water
had no need of government help
were not required to worship the deity
questions.why: The rule worked whether or not anyone could give the reason for it.

questions.q: According to the author, what is the grove's weakness?
opts: It is too small to matter
Its protection lasts only as long as the belief behind it
It cannot be protected by law
questions.why: A protection that rests on belief lasts only as long as the belief does.

questions.q: The last sentence of the passage suggests that:
opts: villages should be fined for cutting trees
belief in deities is declining everywhere
a community's own vigilance protects better than a guard from outside
questions.why: A guard posted from outside is a poorer watchman than a village that believes it is being watched.

questions.q: According to the first paragraph, a public hearing often ends with:
opts: both sides feeling that they were not listened to
a clear decision accepted by all
questions.why: Both sides go home convinced that nothing was heard.

questions.q: The author blames the failure of public hearings mainly on:
opts: the late stage at which they are held
questions.why: The fault lies less with the participants than with the timing.

questions.q: Why is an objection raised at a late hearing 'nearly certain' to be rejected?
opts: Because accepting it would mean abandoning a project already far advanced
Because the law does not allow changes
Because the report is written in advance
questions.why: Only rejection or abandonment remains, and abandonment is unthinkable to those who have come so far.

questions.q: What happens, according to the passage, when residents see a remark of theirs alter a plan?
opts: They bring useful information to later meetings
questions.why: They bring information instead of slogans, because they have learnt that information is used.

questions.q: 'The opposite lesson' taught by a hearing held after the decision is that:
questions.why: Early consultation teaches that information is used; a late hearing teaches that it is not.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: This book is different ______ the one I ordered.
questions.why: In standard usage 'different' is followed by 'from'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Everyone in the three offices ______ expected to carry an identity card.
questions.why: 'Everyone' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: You must submit the form by Friday.
opts: The form must be submitted by Friday.
The form must submitted by Friday.
The form must have submitted by Friday.
The form is must submitted by Friday.
questions.why: With a modal verb the passive is modal + be + past participle.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: You ______ smoke in the hospital; it is strictly forbidden.
questions.why: 'Must not' expresses prohibition. 'Need not' would mean it is unnecessary.

questions.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? I am knowing him (A) / since we were (B) / at school (C) / together (D).
questions.why: 'Know' is not used in the continuous form. With 'since', the present perfect is needed: I have known him.

questions.q: Goa Tourism was awarded in 2025 for which distinction?
questions.why: GPSC's key: Best Wedding Destination. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Which Indian state declared snakebite a notifiable disease in August 2026?
questions.why: GPSC's key: Maharashtra. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which city is home to the start-ups that built the 14-kg mini Earth-observation satellite flown on ISRO's PSLV?
questions.why: GPSC's key: Hyderabad. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Where was India’s first mobile tempered-glass factory inaugurated in 2025?
questions.why: The Optiemus plant in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Who won the 10th men's title at the Indian National Snooker Championship (2025)?
questions.why: Pankaj Advani won his 10th national snooker title. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: Which state became the first to offer AYUSH services in all urban primary health centres?
questions.why: GPSC's key: Madhya Pradesh. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: In how many phases were the Lok Sabha Elections 2024 held?
questions.why: Seven phases, from 19 April to 1 June 2024. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary between
questions.why: Drawn by Cyril Radcliffe in 1947. The McMahon Line is India–China. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Who became the first Indian shooter to win a medal in the men's 25m Rapid Fire at the ISSF World Cup Final (2023)?
questions.why: Anish Bhanwala won bronze in Doha. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2023.

questions.q: Who broke the world record in javelin F64 at the 2023 Asian Para Games?
questions.why: Sumit Antil threw 73.29 m in Hangzhou. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 6, 11, 21, 36, 56, ?
questions.why: The differences are 5, 10, 15, 20, then 25: 56 + 25 = 81.

questions.q: ACE is to BDF as GIK is to:
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: G-H, I-J, K-L.

questions.q: In a certain language 'sun rises east' is written 'pa ko ti', 'east or west' is written 'ti la mu' and 'sun sets west' is written 'pa ru la'. Which word means 'rises'?
questions.why: 'pa' is sun (first and third phrases) and 'ti' is east (first and second), so the remaining word 'ko' is rises.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: January, March and July have 31 days. June has 30.

questions.q: M is the father of N. N is the sister of O. O is the husband of P. How is P related to M?
questions.why: O is M's son and P is O's wife, so P is M's daughter-in-law.

questions.q: A man is facing north. He turns right and walks 20 m, turns right again and walks 20 m, then turns left and walks 10 m. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.why: North, then right to east, right to south, and left back to east.

questions.q: A shoe showroom earns 25% profit after a 25% discount. What would the profit be with only a 10% discount?
questions.why: Marked 100 → sells 75 = 1.25 × cost → cost 60. At 90: profit 30 on 60 = 50%. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Raju's age is 3 more than four times Balu's. In five years Raju will be 1 more than three times Balu's age. What is Raju's present age?
questions.why: 4B + 8 = 3(B + 5) + 1, so B = 8 and R = 35. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Statement: "The recent increase in crime is primarily due to a lack of adequate policing." Conclusions: 1. The government needs more police officers. 2. Crime is directly correlated with the number of police officers.
questions.why: If policing is inadequate, more officers follows; a direct numerical correlation goes beyond the statement. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: Choose the pair that best represents a similar relationship: FISH : SHOAL
questions.why: A shoal is a group of fish; a pack is a group of wolves. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Hahnemann's experiment of 1790, which led him to the law of similars, was made with:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. While translating Cullen's Materia Medica in 1790 he took cinchona himself and developed symptoms like intermittent fever.

questions.q: According to §9, in the healthy condition the material organism is governed by:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §9: in health the spirit-like vital force (dynamis) rules with unbounded sway and keeps all parts in harmonious operation.

questions.q: In Kent's evaluation of mental symptoms, which group ranks highest?
opts: Symptoms of the will (loves, hates, emotions)
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Kent ranks mental symptoms in the order will, understanding, memory.

questions.q: Which miasm has the itch eruption as its primary manifestation?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Psora is the chronic miasm whose primary outward sign is the itch (scabies-like) eruption.

questions.q: A patient who feels his body is enormously enlarged and time passes too slowly, with exaltation and uncontrollable laughter, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Cannabis indica: errors of time and space, exaltation.

questions.q: Homesickness with red cheeks, burning pains like pepper and chilliness in fat, flabby people suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Capsicum: nostalgia with red face; burning like cayenne.

questions.q: Right-sided headache beginning in the occiput, settling over the right eye, rising and falling with the sun, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Sanguinaria is right-sided; Spigelia is left-sided.

questions.q: Sleeplessness from excessive joy or pleasant surprise, with an over-active mind full of ideas, calls for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Coffea: over-excitement of the mind and senses.

questions.q: The remedy Lachesis is prepared from:
opts: the venom of the bushmaster snake
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Lachesis muta, the South American bushmaster.

questions.q: On a prescription, the 'inscription' is the part that gives:
opts: the name and quantity of the medicine
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Superscription (Rx), inscription, subscription (directions to the pharmacist) and signatura (directions to the patient).

questions.q: Boenninghausen's Therapeutic Pocket Book was edited in English in 1891 by:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Timothy F. Allen's edition is the one in common use.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, a desire for salt is found in the chapter:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Food desires and aversions are rubrics under Stomach in Kent.

questions.q: Erb's palsy, with the arm in the 'waiter's tip' position, results from injury to:
opts: the upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Klumpke's palsy is the lower trunk (C8–T1).

questions.q: Wernicke's area, damage to which causes fluent (receptive) aphasia, lies in the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Broca's area (motor aphasia) is in the inferior frontal gyrus.

questions.q: Reed–Sternberg cells are characteristic of:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Large binucleate 'owl's eye' cells, CD15 and CD30 positive.

questions.q: A 'rat-tail' appearance on barium swallow is seen in (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Achalasia gives the bird's-beak appearance.

questions.q: The investigation of choice for acute subarachnoid haemorrhage is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Lumbar puncture for xanthochromia only if CT is negative.

questions.q: Which statement about diabetes is FALSE (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025)?
opts: Acromegaly and Cushing's syndrome can cause diabetes
Most type 2 diabetics die of cardiovascular disease
Type 2 diabetics are more prone to ketoacidosis than type 1
Fasting glucose above 126 mg/dL establishes diabetes
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Type 1 diabetes is the ketosis-prone form.

questions.q: COPD is confirmed on spirometry by a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of less than:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. GOLD criterion; the obstruction is not fully reversible.

questions.q: The 'bagel sign' on ultrasound is seen in (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Tubal ring sign; a molar pregnancy gives a snowstorm appearance.

questions.q: The first visible sign of puberty in girls is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Thelarche usually comes first; menarche comes about 2 years later.

questions.q: The first step in managing a trauma victim is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
opts: securing the airway (with cervical spine protection)
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. ABC: airway first.

questions.q: A whitish membrane on the tonsils that bleeds when scraped off suggests (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. The diphtheria pseudomembrane is adherent and bleeds on removal.

questions.q: According to the demographic cycle, India is in (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Birth rate falling, death rate low.

questions.q: Cadaveric spasm differs from rigor mortis because it:
opts: occurs instantly at death and preserves the last act, such as grip on a weapon
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Medicolegally important in suicide, drowning and so on.
